verses.text: This is the message of judgment against Tyre. Cry out, you ships of Tarshish! For Tyre is destroyed, with no house left and no harbor to enter. The news has reached them from the land of Cyprus.
Be silent, you people who live on the coast, you traders of Sidon, who grew rich from those who sail the sea.
On the great waters came the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile. That was Tyre's income. She was the marketplace of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the strong fortress of the sea says, "I have never been in labor or given birth. I have never raised sons or brought up daughters."
When the news reaches Egypt, they will be in great pain over the report about Tyre.
Sail across to Tarshish! Cry out, you people who live on the coast!
Is this your city of celebration, the ancient city, whose people traveled to settle in faraway lands?
Who planned this against Tyre, the city that gave out crowns, whose traders were princes, whose merchants were honored all over the earth?
The LORD of Armies planned it, to bring down the pride of all its glory and to humble all who were honored on earth.
Go through your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish. There is no harbor anymore.
The LORD has stretched out his hand over the sea and made kingdoms shake. He has given orders to destroy the strong cities of Canaan.
He said, "You will celebrate no more, crushed virgin daughter of Sidon. Get up, cross over to Cyprus. Even there you will find no rest."
Look at the land of the Babylonians. That people is no more. The Assyrians made it a place for desert creatures. They built their siege towers, tore down its palaces, and made it a ruin.
Cry out, you ships of Tarshish, for your fortress is destroyed!
On that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the length of a king's life. At the end of seventy years, Tyre will be like the prostitute in the song:
"Pick up a harp and walk around the city, you forgotten prostitute. Play sweetly, sing many songs, so that you will be remembered."
At the end of seventy years, the LORD will deal with Tyre. She will go back to earning her pay and will sell herself to all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

But her profits and her pay will be set apart for the LORD. They will not be stored up or saved. Her profits will go to those who live in the presence of the LORD, so they will have plenty of food and fine clothes.
